translations.whyIntro: Communication science and framing research demonstrate that how political actors are perceived is substantially shaped by the visual signals used to represent them in news formats.
translations.whyCard1: In colour psychology, blue is universally linked to calm, credibility, and objectivity. It is the hallmark colour of international peacekeeping bodies and European institutions. Adopting a party's self-chosen branding without critique creates a subconscious softening effect toward anti-constitutional tendencies.
translations.whyCard2: In German political iconography, brown unequivocally signifies völkisch nationalism. Responsible information graphics must not uncritically reproduce partisan branding, but must transparently reflect court-documented unconstitutional extremism.

translations.editorialPolicyIntro: This site follows an informational, documentation-led approach. To ensure clarity and accountability, our standards are transparently outlined:
translations.editorialPolicyRule1: Primary sources first: We prioritize direct links to scientific research, court rulings, and independent newsrooms.
translations.editorialPolicyRule2: Context over slogans: All topics are contextualized with dates, institutional background, and analytical depth.

translations.editorialPolicyCorrectionsBody: If you identify a factual inaccuracy, please get in touch via the channels provided in the legal notice. Substantive notes will be verified and addressed promptly.

sprache.desc: Far-right movements deliberately adopt conventional, calming colour codes to soften their radical image and project bourgeois respectability into mainstream society.
While European blue stands for the rule of law, international cooperation, and open borders, a nationalist party exploits the exact same colour to advocate ethno-national isolation and 'Dexit'.
Behind a placid blue facade lies a political platform confirmed by higher administrative courts to attack human dignity (Art. 1 Basic Law) and normalize racist exclusion.

symbolik.desc: The blue field symbolizes the unification of the continent based on the rule of law, universal human rights, and overcoming aggressive nationalism.
Chosen by the United Nations as an international emblem of non-partisan peacekeeping, de-escalation, and protecting vulnerable civilians from authoritarian violence.
In cultural history, the universal emblem of cosmopolitanism, the search for truth, intellectual freedom, and human solidarity across borders.

oeffentlich.to: TO: Editorial Boards of ARD-aktuell & ZDF
oeffentlich.subject: Re: Visual Framing, Journalistic Duty of Contextualization, and Impartiality
body: Public service broadcasters bear an indispensable constitutional responsibility to provide truthful, unvarnished information to the public.

When parties whose regional chapters are judicially confirmed as proven right-wing extremist, and whose federal body is classified as a suspected extremist threat, are depicted in election graphics in the same uncontextualized blue as democratic institutions, a subconscious normalization effect is produced (Visual Framing).

We urge you to enhance your editorial standards: Impartiality does not mean passive replication of partisan PR. Newsroom diagrams and reports must visually reflect documented unconstitutional extremism through distinct labels, warning badges, and contextual annotations.

privat.to: TO: Editorial Boards of ProSiebenSat.1, RTL Group & dpa
privat.subject: Re: Default Colour Schemes, Infographic Distribution, and Journalistic Distance
body: Your news broadcasts and wire agency feeds reach millions of citizens every day and decisively shape public opinion.
Uncritically passing along soothing self-selected branding colours for ethno-nationalist and racist political actors blurs the vital line between democratic pluralism and authoritarian extremism.
We call on private newsrooms to critically evaluate graphical standards and avoid the unexamined replication of far-right corporate identity, prioritizing clear visual contextualization.

rundfunkrat.to: TO: ARD Broadcasting Councils & ZDF Television Council
rundfunkrat.subject: Re: Program Oversight Regarding Visual Framing Effects and Constitutional Diligence
body: As independent oversight bodies of public service broadcasting, you are entrusted with safeguarding journalistic quality standards and democratic core values.

Visual presentation in news programming leaves a profound subconscious imprint. Presenting radical and racist actors within an unobtrusive default spectrum contradicts the mission of enlightened journalism.
We urge you to demand binding guidelines for the differentiated, fact-based visual classification of anti-constitutional forces in graphical reporting.

faqs.q: Why is the party colour blue problematic here?
faqs.a: Farbpsychologisch steht Blau für Stabilität, Ruhe und Neutralität – it is also the colour of the UN and the EU. When media uncritically mirrors the self-chosen colour of a party with proven right-wing extremist factions, this calming sentiment is unconsciously transferred to the party's image (Visual Framing). This normalizes unconstitutional and racist policies while concealing their threat to democracy and economic prosperity.

faqs.q: Wouldn't changing the colour violate journalistic neutrality?
faqs.a: No. Journalistic neutrality requires objective contextualization, not passive multiplication of PR. The Federal Constitutional Court requires media to report reality truthfully. This includes transparently marking court-confirmed unconstitutional extremism rather than uncritically waving through partisan branding.

faqs.q: What is the goal of this initiative?
faqs.a: We aim to inform the public: The AfD is not a conventional conservative party, but an ethno-nationalist, racist force that enacts policies for billionaires and oligarchs at the expense of working people, pensioners, and low-income families. Our petition calls on media not to mask this reality behind soothing visual codes.
An independent civil society initiative for democratic vigilance, media ethics, and constitutional awareness, launched via Change.org.

science.sectionSub: Fact Sheet: Visual Framing, Editorial Contextualization, and Constitutional Reality

foundations.title: The Psychological Dimension of 'Visual Framing' (Halo Effect)

points.label: Colour Psychology of Blue
points.text: Empirical studies consistently link shades of blue with seriousness, de-escalation, and trustworthiness – which is why institutions like the United Nations and the European Union employ this colour.

points.label: Cognitive Dissonance & Normalization
points.text: When an actor whose regional chapters are classified as proven right-wing extremists is visualized in reassuring blue, a downplaying effect occurs: peaceful aesthetics dull public vigilance toward constitutional and racist threats.

points.label: The taz Precedent & Free Press
points.text: The choice of independent newsrooms such as taz to visually distinguish AfD results demonstrates that graphic design is an expression of journalistic judgment, not an automated transmission belt.

points.label: Responsible Contextualization
points.text: Media organizations are not obligated to amplify party marketing. Due diligence requires that reporting on extremist activities is not neutralized by soothing design defaults. Clear labels and contextual footnotes are standard editorial tools.

objections.title: Objection 1: 'The neutrality mandate demands identical formal treatment.'

rebuttals.label: Substantive Rather Than Mere Formal Balance
rebuttals.text: Constitutional jurisprudence requires media to provide substantive context. Journalistic duty includes transparently identifying differences in constitutional fidelity between political parties.

rebuttals.label: Findings of Intelligence Agencies as Objective Facts
rebuttals.text: Court-confirmed classifications by constitutional protection agencies (OVG Münster 2024) are verified facts. Visually marking these facts fulfills the legal mandate for truthful and accurate reporting.

rebuttals.label: Broadcasting Autonomy
rebuttals.text: The freedom of broadcasting guaranteed in the Basic Law (Art. 5(1) sentence 2) protects newsrooms from having to replicate party PR concepts unfiltered.

rebuttals.label: Duty of Journalistic Distance
rebuttals.text: Party marketing serves electoral strategy. Professional ethics demand maintaining independence rather than uncritically amplifying image-crafting tactics.

rebuttals.label: Informing the Public
rebuttals.text: Diagrams must provide genuine orientation. A presentation mode that flattens extremist stances behind calming colour codes undermines this educational mission.

objections.title: Objection 3: 'This feeds the party's victim narrative.'

rebuttals.label: Structural Self-Victimization
rebuttals.text: Media analyses demonstrate that populist actors utilize the grievance narrative regardless of actual editorial design choices.

rebuttals.label: Transparency Over Timidity
rebuttals.text: Editorial choices should not be inhibited by fear of partisan backlash. Objectively and scientifically grounded standards are the firmest foundation for journalistic credibility.

policyDangers.title: Social Welfare & Inequality
policyDangers.description: Economic and social analyses confirm: The AfD operates as a lobby for multimillionaires, severely penalizing low-wage workers, retirees, and families.
points: The AfD Paradox (DIW Berlin): The tax and welfare platform yields massive tax breaks for the top 1% of earners, while lower and middle-income households suffer net losses.
Rejection and erosion of the statutory minimum wage and opposition to collective bargaining protections, harming working-class families across structurally weak regions.
Demands to eliminate wealth and inheritance taxes for the super-rich while mandating forced labor ('citizen work') for social benefit recipients.
policyDangers.citation: German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin) — The AfD Paradox (2023)

policyDangers.title: Economy & Prosperity
policyDangers.description: Nationalist isolationism and leaving the EU would dismantle Germany's industrial core and destroy millions of livelihoods.
points: IW Cologne (2024): A German exit from the EU ('Dexit') would trigger a 5.6% GDP contraction within 5 years (approx. €690 billion lost) and eliminate 2.5 million jobs.
Exacerbating severe skilled labor shortages through xenophobic hostility and international deterrence of qualified specialists.
Threatening the export sector, which accounts directly for one in every four German jobs.
policyDangers.citation: German Economic Institute (IW Cologne) — Economic Impact of EU Exit (2024)

policyDangers.title: Press Freedom & Rule of Law
policyDangers.description: Systematic harassment of independent media, intimidation of journalists, and attacks on constitutional checks and balances.
points: Court-ordered injunctions preventing the exclusion of journalists from party congresses and election events (Erfurt and Munich Regional Courts).
Aggressive campaigns aimed at defunding and dismantling public service broadcasting to replace it with partisan propaganda channels.
Threat of authoritarian capture similar to illiberal regimes that have subordinated public media and silenced judicial independence.
policyDangers.citation: Regional Courts Erfurt & Munich I — Emergency Rulings on Press Freedom

policyDangers.title: Constitutional Order & Institutions
policyDangers.description: Appellate court rulings and intelligence assessments prove a systematic assault on human dignity and democratic pluralism.
points: Higher Administrative Court Münster (May 2024): Fully upheld the federal classification of the AfD and its youth wing as suspected extremist entities.
State branches in Thüringen, Saxony, and Saxony-Anhalt officially designated by intelligence services as 'proven right-wing extremist'.
Björn Höcke criminally convicted multiple times for deliberately uttering banned Nazi SA slogans (LG Halle 2024).
policyDangers.citation: Higher Administrative Court NRW (Case 5 A 1218/22) / Regional Court Halle (2024)

policyDangers.title: Security & Racism
policyDangers.description: Mass deportation fantasies targeting millions of residents and rising threats from right-wing extremist networks.
points: Potsdam secret meeting (Correctiv investigation): Master plan to expel millions of residents ('remigration'), explicitly including naturalized German citizens.
Violation of Human Dignity (Art. 1 Basic Law): The party's ethnic-völkisch ideology degrades citizens with immigrant backgrounds into second-class subjects.
Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA): Right-wing politically motivated crimes remain the single greatest domestic security threat in Germany.
policyDangers.citation: Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) PMK / Federal Constitutional Court (BVerfGE 144, 20)

policyDangers.title: Geopolitics & Alliances
policyDangers.description: Close alignment with authoritarian foreign regimes to undermine European and transatlantic security.
points: Federal Prosecutor General investigations into allegations of bribery, covert funding, and espionage for Russia and China within AfD circles.
Leading role in establishing the radical-nationalist ESN faction in the European Parliament to weaken democratic European unity.
Demands to dismantle Western collective security alliances while actively justifying aggressive wars of conquest.
